findings.title: unsubscribe crashes with NoMethodError when the user has no TopicUser row
findings.body: `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil when the user has never interacted with the topic (no topic_users record). The next line `tu.notification_level` then raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. Emails are sent to users who may have no TopicUser row for the topic, for example users who were notified via a watch/category setting without a row, so the link can be clicked in a state with no record. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, ...)` or find-or-create the record before reading it.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe happens on GET, so mail scanners and link prefetchers can mute topics
findings.body: The unsubscribe action changes notification_level on a GET request (route `get "t/:topic_id/unsubscribe"`) and also skips the xhr check. Email security scanners, link previewers, or prefetching clients that follow links in the notification email will silently mute the topic without user intent. Mutating actions should use POST (with a confirmation page for the GET), or the request should be otherwise protected.

findings.title: Unsubscribe from watching/tracking only drops to regular, which still sends emails
findings.body: When the current level is above regular (tracking or watching), the action sets it to regular rather than muted. Regular users still receive notifications for replies and quotes, so the link described as 'stop receiving notifications for this topic' does not stop them. The behavior also depends on the current level in a way that is not a clear unsubscribe. The intended semantics should be defined and the mapping fixed (likely always muted).

findings.title: Direct tu.save! bypasses TopicUser.change, so reason, timestamps and MessageBus update are skipped
findings.body: The unsubscribe path updates notification_level with `tu.save!` instead of `TopicUser.change`. This skips setting notifications_changed_at and notifications_reason_id (the user-changed reason), and it does not publish the notification_level_change on MessageBus, so an open browser tab keeps showing the old level. The rest of the codebase uses TopicUser.change for this.

findings.title: List-Unsubscribe header still points to the preferences page, not the per-topic unsubscribe URL
findings.body: In message_builder.rb the List-Unsubscribe header is built from `template_args[:user_preferences_url]`. The new per-topic unsubscribe_url is only added to the body text. Mail clients' one-click unsubscribe therefore sends the user to global preferences, and the feature's per-topic option is not exposed through the header. The header should use the topic's unsubscribe_url when it is provided.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url, which callers that set add_unsubscribe_link may not pass
findings.body: The string now interpolates `%{unsubscribe_url}`. Any build_email call with add_unsubscribe_link: true that does not pass unsubscribe_url (the message builder merges only the opts given) will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument when the body or HTML part is rendered. The only caller updated is send_notification_email; any other caller of add_unsubscribe_link breaks. Either pass a default or guard the interpolation.

findings.title: No tests for the new unsubscribe action or the per-topic link in the body
findings.body: The spec change only adds an unsubscribe_url argument to an existing case and asserts only that the List-Unsubscribe header is present and the preferences URL is in the body. Nothing checks that the per-topic unsubscribe URL appears in the body or that the link is correct. The new TopicsController#unsubscribe action (its nil-TopicUser case, the notification level transitions, the 301 redirect on slug mismatch, and the access check for anonymous users) has no controller spec.

findings.title: Misspelled property name 'stopNotificiationsText' used across controller and template
findings.body: The property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (with an extra 'fi') in both the controller and the hbs template. The name is consistent between them, so it works, but it is a misspelling that will be copied elsewhere. Rename it to `stopNotificationsText` in both files.

findings.title: Unrelated refactor of topic-from-params route is bundled into the unsubscribe feature PR
findings.body: The diff rewrites `topic-from-params.js.es6` (var to const, moved declarations, reformatting, and a switch from function syntax to method syntax) without any behavior change related to unsubscribe. The same applies to the dropdown-button, topic_user.rb, and notification.html.erb reformatting. These changes add review load and risk unrelated regressions. They should be split out.

findings.title: Existing summary route silently loses its post_number constraint
findings.body: The `t/:slug/:topic_id/summary` and `t/:topic_id/summary` routes were modified: the `post_number: /\d+/` constraint was removed from the topic_id summary route and the slug summary route's constraint was altered, and the moderator-liked/wordpress lines were reordered. These are unrelated to unsubscribe and change matching behavior of existing URLs. Revert the unrelated route edits.

findings.title: unsubscribe_url is built from url, which ignores the Discourse.base_uri path
findings.body: `unsubscribe_url` returns `"#{url}/unsubscribe"`, and `url` uses `Discourse.base_url` plus the slug and id. That is consistent with `url`, but the controller redirect uses `unsubscribe_url` (absolute), while the rest of the controller uses relative_url. Mixing absolute and relative URLs for the redirect could be fine, but the choice is unexplained and no test covers it.
